title: Book Two · Chapter 130: The High Water Line
story:
The rain ends on Sunday morning. Dad and Ronan walk toward the square. The blue bike stays at home because the paths are wet.

Near the river wall, a dark line marks the stone. Dad keeps Ronan on the broad path, well away from the edge.

“Look at that,” he says.

“The water reached there?”

“During the heavy rain, yes.”

Ronan compares the mark with Dad's knee. It is higher than he expects.

“Can we go closer?”

“No. We can see it from here.”

They stand back while a worker crosses with a long broom. The worker clears leaves from a drain. Dad asks if the path ahead is open.

“Only to the square,” the worker says. “The lower path is closed.”

Dad thanks him and turns toward the square. Ronan can see the steps to the lower path. There is a rope across them.

At the square, the ball has a new bounce on the damp ground. It skips sideways and hits Dad's shoe.

“An excellent pass,” Dad says.

“You were not moving.”

“I planned that.”

They play on the dry half. Ronan scores twice between two marks. Dad gets one lucky goal when the ball rolls off the side of his foot.

“That counts,” Dad says.

“You did not plan it.”

“I can plan and be lucky.”

Ronan laughs. He picks up the ball and looks toward the river wall.

“I wanted to see the line close.”

“I know.”

“You always say no near the water.”

“Some places need that answer.”

Ronan rubs a wet mark from the ball. He looks again at the rope across the steps. The lower path is wet. Dad keeps walking toward the dry square.

On the way home, they meet Leo and his parents near the wide road. Leo is back from the other town earlier than expected. He has a paper bag in his hand.

“Food report,” he tells Ronan.

He gives him a small round cake. Dad accepts one from Leo's father.

“School?” Ronan asks quietly.

“Big. Far from my aunt's house. We are still talking.”

Leo looks at the ball. “Five minutes?”

His parents agree to a short stop at the square. The two boys run to the dry entrance and wait there. Dad walks behind with the cakes.

Ronan's first throw is too hard. Leo catches it anyway.

“Same arm,” Leo says.

“New cake.”

They play until Leo's father calls. Ronan eats the cake on the walk home. He does not need to ask about the other school again today.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

drain＝排水口；rope＝绳子；bounce＝弹跳；damp＝潮湿的。

## 理解问题

1. 父子怎样遵守河边关闭安排？
2. Leo对外地学校的安排有最终答案了吗？

## 读句子

**Dad / thanks him / and turns toward the square.** Dad／向他道谢／转向广场。
